events.text: Every child in the village is told the story of {legend}, who walked through the Last Door. When your grandmother tells it, something in your chest aches.

effects.log: The third time, you correct her about the colour of the gate. She stares at you for a long time.

choices.text: Pretend to be {legend} in the yard

effects.log: You play the Ascended One with a stick for a sword. Some of your moves are uncannily right.

events.text: The village children play 'The Last Door': one child is {legend}, the rest are the Ten Greatest trying to stop {legend_them}. Nobody ever wants to be the Ten Greatest.

effects.log: You win every game. The other children say it is not fair. You cannot explain why it feels like remembering.

choices.text: Be the Ten Greatest, for once

effects.log: You lose on purpose, very convincingly. An old man watching laughs until he cries.

events.text: In the square of the provincial capital stands a statue of {legend}, one foot on a cloud. The face is wrong. The stance is right.

choices.text: Stand before it and copy the stance

effects.log: Your body slides into it as if it had been waiting a hundred years. Passers-by stop and stare.
It seems like the kind of offering {legend_they} would have liked. You are not sure how you know.

events.text: A teahouse storyteller tells the tale of {legend}. He gets almost everything wrong: {legend_they} was taller, braver, and never lost a fight.

effects.log: 'And how would you know?' the whole teahouse asks. You find you have no good answer.

choices.text: Let the legend be bigger than the truth

effects.log: Stories are allowed to grow. You buy the storyteller a drink.

events.text: A small shrine on the mountain road honours {legend}. Travellers leave pebbles on the altar, one for each wish.

effects.log: The air around the shrine is strangely familiar. For an hour, your energy moves as it once did, long ago.

choices.text: Leave a pebble and walk on

effects.log: A small wish. It is yours.

events.text: In a library, behind a glass cabinet, lies a copy of the {legend_manual}. The librarian says no one has ever understood the last chapter.

effects.log: You read the last chapter first. You understand it at once, and then you understand why: you wrote it. (Grade 5 methods open in Arts.)

choices.text: Leave it for someone who needs it

effects.log: Some things should be found by others.

events.text: The {legend_sect} keeps a hall for {legend}, with {legend_their} old sword on the wall and a portrait nobody is allowed to dust.

effects.log: The sword on the wall hums when you walk past. A monk drops his broom.
They refuse, of course. Then the sword falls off the wall into your hands. Nobody knows what to say.

events.text: A charismatic swindler claims to be the reincarnation of {legend} and is collecting silver from the faithful.

effects.log: You ask him three questions only {legend} could answer. He cannot. You can. The crowd goes very quiet.
The faithful will find out. They always do.

events.text: A master of a small school proudly tells you his teacher's teacher's teacher was taught by {legend}.

effects.log: Five generations have worn the forms smooth. You can still see the original under them.
He tries it your way. His eyes go wide. 'Where did you learn that?'

events.text: The murim still measures every great master against {legend}, the First Under Heaven of a century ago.

effects.log: Let them measure. One day they will measure against you.
It is strange to feel competitive with a statue.

events.text: You climb the peak where {legend} walked through the Last Door. At the top, the air shimmers, as if a door had been left open a crack.

effects.log: For one breath you remember everything: every life, every fight, the light between the clouds. Then it is gone, but your energy is not.
Not yet. The door will wait.

events.text: In a dream, an old master with your own eyes sits across a Go board from you. 'You took the long way back,' {legend_they} says.

effects.log: 'Do it differently this time.' You wake up and know exactly what that means.

choices.text: Ask if it was worth it

effects.log: {legend} only smiles, and places a stone.
